context.summary: Use stylistically related covers as discovery bridges to originals; test whether listeners actually convert.
Explore Hindi-rock identity across Netherlands, Suriname/Caribbean, UK and India; regional affinity remains a hypothesis, not verified audience analytics.
Test immediate vocal/performance openings and distinct emotional moments: direct gaze, intimate phrase, chorus and climax. Historical timestamps require mapping to the current asset SHA and timebase.
Explore several distinct short cuts from one performance plus full-length releases. No historical format classification establishes current platform eligibility.

Historical options converge on dark charcoal, antique gold, face-first hierarchy and readable restrained typography. Preserve the currently locked baseline; these are context, not redesign authorization.
Favor stable intimate passages and sparse musically justified motion. Historical FX cues require actual-asset inspection and fresh validation; no blanket shake/flash preset.
Consider selective translation windows and clean instrumental breathing spaces; check baked-in captions and current platform overlays before placing text.
Adapt calls-to-action and presentation to platform and audience, with restrained end cards and mobile-readable thumbnails. Current UI geometry and policies require fresh checks.
Historical staged cadence suggests beginning with 14-day releases and accelerating only after measured capacity and traction. It is not a schedule instruction or publication approval.
Track retention, watch time, click-through, subscriber conversion and catalog lift across explicit review windows. Thresholds must be recalibrated with real analytics.
Bind master, derivative/hook, campaign, experiment and eventual platform identifiers to outcomes. Historical ABSENT-field claims are not a current system audit.
Keep model analysis, synthesis, actual-asset hashes and human authorization separate. Historical architecture suggestions do not replace the existing Event Ledger/Reducer.
Source calls a rule 80% but describes 75%; this contradiction cannot weaken the current hard 80% constraint.
Earlier continuous-English advice conflicts with later selective-caption advice; retain both as hypotheses and judge the actual asset independently.
